trial_court: Additional District Judge, Delhi (HMA No. 447 of 2000)
facts_of_case: Appellant and respondent were married in Delhi; respondent showed no interest in household work, was disrespectful to the appellant, and insisted on returning to Delhi after childbirth. Appellant sought divorce on grounds of cruelty and desertion.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove it.
legal_principles.held: It was pointed out by the respondent that the appellant had treated her with cruelty and had turned her out from the matrimonial home along with her infant children since she declined to fulfill the dowry demand of the appellant.

legal_principles.principle: A party's decision to withdraw a petition does not necessarily mean they have abandoned their claim.
legal_principles.held: In rejoinder, it was pointed out by the appellant that he had decided to withdraw the application for restitution of conjugal rights at the time of filing the petition for divorce; that the respondent had deserted the matrimonial home on her own accord and that there was no scope for the parties to live together as husband and wife.

outcome.final_order: Trial court's judgment and decree dated 6.5.2003 were upheld, dismissing the appellant's petition for divorce.
